1,000 animals: 56.19 → 55.57 ms CPU per tick. 63% fewer pen-mates passed to the final movement check. Overall CPU differences are small and mixed; no consistent speedup established.

10,000 exact movement comparisons · four full-scene day/night checks · exact save/restore and resource-state parity

Method, hidden interiors & limitations

Each of four saved scenes runs six interleaved pairs of 40 fixed ticks. The chart shows median browser-thread CPU time per tick using Chrome threadTicks timing, with rendering suspended. This isolates behavior work from frame submission and OS scheduling waits; it does not establish an FPS gain. All identities, movement decisions, needs, resources and schedules match the baseline.

Workers inside opaque buildings already use coarse offsite behavior. Hidden bodies now skip unnecessary pose interpolation. Open pens retain full movement fidelity. A spatial-grid experiment was rejected because its overhead did not show reliable benefit for these pen sizes. The deployed change reuses one conservative, ordered nearby-peer list for steering and final swept collision checks.

The 520/1,000-animal expanded boards retain existing terrain/access and care/accounting limitations. Zero collisions in these short checks is not a long-run capacity guarantee. Full measurements and checks · Renderer FPS comparison
